**Potential Duplicate Found:**

  - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/24988

Both PRs address the same underlying issue: preventing unintended option submission when dragging to select text on question prompts in the TUI. PR #24988 appears to be a related fix targeting the same problem. You should check if one supersedes the other or if they address different aspects of the issue.

Here is an English version:

---

On Windows, if the user environment registry contains bad entries, the assembled environment block can cause `CreateProcessW` to fail with **ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87)**. Logging for this path should be more detailed so it is easier to see what went wrong—especially when the problem comes from system environment variables.

The fix was to remove these four bad values under the user environment key:

```bat
reg delete "HKCU\Environment" /v DriverArcL /f
reg delete "HKCU\Environment" /v DriverAnoD /f
reg delete "HKCU\Environment" /v DriverAnoM /f
reg delete "HKCU\Environment" /v XiuMaster_v1_button_hotkey /f
```

After deleting those entries, the embedded terminal worked again.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #24476: Same root cause — client-generated message IDs sort before server-generated assistant IDs when there is clock skew between client and server, causing the prompt loop to exit early without generating a response to follow-up messages.

I hit the same issue. #25024 - the server's clock is ahead of the client's clock. The key problem is the message id:
- Both client and server can generate the id (server trusts the msg id from client blindly)
- The msg id is used in many places to sort the conversation (instead of using parent ids, or use "created_at" timestamp)

LLM generated details:

### 1) Observed mismatch: `message.id` ordering vs `time.created`
In failed cases, `message.id` lexical order does not match `message.time.created` order across user and assistant turns.

### 2) Two ID generation origins
- **Client-generated user IDs**:
  - `packages/app/src/components/prompt-input/submit.ts` (`Identifier.ascending("message")`)
- **Server-generated assistant IDs**:
  - `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` (`MessageID.ascending()`)

### 3) Ordering assumptions in core logic
OpenCode relies on ID-based ordering/comparison (not only `time.created`) in multiple places, e.g.:
- prompt loop condition comparing user/assistant IDs:
  - `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` (`lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id`)
- binary-search insertion/lookups over ID-sorted arrays:
  - `packages/core/src/util/binary.ts`
  - `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/event-reducer.ts`
  - `packages/app/src/context/sync.tsx`

So correctness depends on IDs sharing a single monotonic timeline.

### 4) Why this fails with clock skew
If user IDs come from client time and assistant IDs come from server time, skew can make one side’s IDs “jump ahead”.  
Then ID comparisons no longer represent actual turn chronology, and run/loop behavior becomes inconsistent.

----

Proposed Fix (suggestion)

Maintain a **monotonic server-side ID floor**:

1. Server tracks the highest seen message ID per session (including client-provided user IDs).
2. When generating any new server message ID, ensure it is strictly greater than that floor.
3. If an incoming client message ID is greater than current floor, advance floor to that value.
4. Optionally, reject or normalize client IDs that violate format/order guarantees.

This keeps all IDs in one monotonic sequence even under clock skew.

The frontend (client) needs to do a similar thing in case the client's clock is ahead.

the /usage endpoint being the single source of truth is the right call. the trap people fall into is parsing rate-limit headers or counting local tokens, then their numbers drift from what claude.ai actually shows. ccusage reads jsonl logs, claude-code-usage-monitor estimates, neither sees the server quota anthropic actually enforces. only the internal endpoint that powers claude.ai/settings/usage gives you the real 5h and weekly windows. one note on the 401 question, claude's session cookie expires silently and you wont know until the next fetch returns nothing useful, surfacing a reauth hint inline beats a refresh loop because the cookie path is browser-bound anyway.
